title: Wasting less food
description: Food waste costs money and the planet — the fridge habits that cut both.

body.heading: Shop your kitchen first
paragraphs: Before shopping, look at what you already have and plan around it. The most wasted food is often the food bought twice, or bought for a meal that never happened.
A short list, written after that kitchen check, is the single best defence against both waste and overspending.

body.heading: Store it like you mean it
paragraphs: Learn the few storage rules that matter: keep the fridge cold, store herbs and salads with a dry paper towel, freeze bread and leftovers you will not reach in time. Freezing is a pause button, not a bin.
An 'eat me first' shelf or box in the fridge gathers soon-to-expire items into one visible place, so they get used in time.

body.heading: Love your leftovers
paragraphs: Cook once, eat twice: make extra portions deliberately and lunch is sorted. Odd leftovers become soup, fried rice, omelettes, or wraps — flexible dishes that welcome whatever needs using.

takeaway: Plan from what you have, freeze what you cannot reach, and give leftovers a starring role.
